reasons: No test is visible for this file.
Address matching relies on a hand-kept list that can drift from the real routes.

terms.meaning: A short, URL-safe name for an item, such as nuclear, used inside web addresses.
The part of the app that maps web addresses to screens.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for industry context
sections.what: Brings in the router hook for reading the current address and the industry lookup.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are needed to read the address and identify the industry.

sections.name: IndustryPaths
sections.title: Shape of industry page addresses
sections.what: Defines the set of named page addresses that each industry provides, such as its explore, pipeline, and project pages.
sections.why: Gives every screen one shared set of names, so no screen builds its own address strings.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new page type means adding it here and in every industry's path builder.

sections.name: industryPaths
sections.title: Building page addresses for an industry
sections.what: Returns the full set of page addresses for one industry. Nuclear gets the older unscoped addresses, and every other industry gets addresses under its own name.
sections.why: The comment says the original workspace was built for nuclear first, so nuclear keeps its old addresses.
sections.watch_out: Nuclear and other industries use different address shapes, so a change to one branch does not affect the other.

sections.name: projectHref
sections.title: Link to one project
sections.what: Builds the web address for a single project page. Nuclear projects use the old address shape and others use the industry-based shape.
sections.why: Same reason as the path builder: nuclear keeps its legacy layout.
sections.watch_out: Project IDs are placed into the address without encoding, so an ID with special characters could break the link.

sections.name: NUCLEAR_LEGACY_PREFIXES
sections.title: Old nuclear address prefixes
sections.what: Lists the older nuclear-only address starts, such as explore, pipeline, and projects, that have no industry name in them.
sections.why: Lets the app recognize these older pages as nuclear pages.
sections.watch_out: The list must match the nuclear addresses in the path builder. A missing entry means that page loses its industry context.

sections.name: useIndustryContext
sections.title: Finding the current industry from the address
sections.what: Looks at the current web address and decides which industry is open. It returns nothing for the landing page, login page, or unknown industries.
sections.why: Other screens need to know which industry they belong to without being told.
sections.watch_out: If the industry lookup does not know a slug, this returns nothing, so the page loses its industry context silently.

summary: Works out which industry the current web page belongs to and gives the matching page addresses for that industry.
purpose: Lets any screen know which industry is open and build correct links for it.
why: The app has an older nuclear-only layout with unscoped addresses, and newer industries use addresses that start with the industry name. This file hides that difference from the rest of the app.
how: Reads the current address. If it starts with an industry name, it takes that name as the industry. If it matches an old nuclear-only address, it uses nuclear. Then it checks the industry exists and builds the list of page addresses for it.
inputs: The current browser address from the router, the list of old nuclear addresses, and the industry lookup from shared industries.
outputs: An object with the industry slug, the industry details, and the page address list. It returns nothing when the page is not tied to an industry.
risks: A new nuclear page that is missing from the old address list will not be recognized as nuclear. An address that looks like an industry but is not in the lookup returns nothing.
debug: If a page shows the wrong industry, print the current address and compare it with the old address list. If links point to the wrong place, compare the output of the path builder for that industry.
